title: Take one learning step
summary: The learning rate sets how big a weight update is. Subtracting a small amount in the slope direction can reduce the loss.
introduction: The learning rate sets how big a weight update is. Subtracting a small amount in the slope direction can reduce the loss. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: The learning rate sets how big a weight update is. Subtracting a small amount in the slope direction can reduce the loss.

blocks.code:
weight = 5.0
rate = 0.1
slope = 2 * (weight - 3)
weight = weight - rate * slope
print(round(weight, 2))
blocks.title: Take one learning step

blocks.text: The output is 4.6. The update subtracts 0.4 from 5. This brings the weight closer to the target 3 for this simple loss.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Try rate 0.2 and find the new weight.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A larger learning rate is not always better; it can overshoot.
